sources.entry: authsome by agentrhq - Credential gateway for AI agents. Log in once via Oauth2 or API Key. Every agent stays authenticated — headless, no SaaS, agents never see your credentials.

summary.one_liner: Authsome is an open-source credential gateway that stores OAuth2 and API-key credentials encrypted and injects them into agent HTTP requests through a proxy, so agents never handle the secrets directly.
summary.what_it_does: Authsome is a CLI and daemon that holds login credentials for external services in one encrypted store. Users authenticate once through browser PKCE, device code, or a browser bridge for API key entry. Agents then run commands prefixed with `authsome run --`, and a local auth proxy injects fresh headers into matching requests, matched by provider api_url such as api.openai.com. Tokens are refreshed before expiry. The README says secrets are kept out of the child process environment. It supports multiple accounts per provider and lists bundled OAuth2 and API-key providers. It can also run as a persistent Docker daemon with a Postgres backend, and onboarding can import API keys from a .env file. The README names adapters for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, LangChain, LlamaIndex, the OpenAI Agents SDK, and the Anthropic SDK.
use_cases: give an AI agent access to gmail or github without sharing passwords
run headless agents in CI, cron, or SSH sessions with valid API tokens
replace hardcoded API tokens in environment variables
rotate and manage API keys across many agents from one place
check service data such as a Stripe balance from an agent task
self-host a shared credential daemon for a team
notable: Agent-side `authsome run --` wrapper injects credentials at request time without placing secrets in the child process environment
Login once through browser PKCE, device code, or a browser bridge; agents then run headlessly
Self-hostable persistent daemon in Docker with no Python needed on the host
Multi-account support per provider with built-in providers requiring no config
Ships a skill installable via npx skills for Claude, Codex, Cursor and other agents
caveats: Requires Python 3.13 or newer for the CLI install path

Self-hosting requires setting several secret environment variables (master key, UI session key, Postgres password) and a public HTTPS base URL for hosted use; TLS termination is left to the user per the self-hosting guide
Roadmap and some integration details are only on the external website, not in the README
